title: Cost Drift Investigator: tenant shadowing, automated rollback policies, and zipper quantizer
author: Samir Patel
description:
Motivation: We see recurring micro-regressions where tenant-level unit economics drift upward after model/quant/profile changes; operators currently detect these manually via ad-hoc dashboards. This PR introduces an automated 'Cost Drift Investigator' that (1) runs shadow evaluations of candidate quant/profile changes per tenant, (2) synthesizes unit-econ deltas with confidence bands, and (3) enforces safe rollback policies when drift exceeds thresholds. We also introduce a gradual quantization strategy ("zipper quantizer") that steps precision down in controlled phases with live telemetry gating.

What this PR does (summary): 
- Tenant shadowing: pipeline to run candidate quant/profile variants in parallel (no user-visible outputs) and compute per-tenant cost-per-1000-tokens, latency p50/p95, and quality delta (based on existing eval harness signals). Shadow runs are stored as lightweight traces and sampled to control egress cost.
- Drift detection engine: rolling-window statistical detector that flags regressions based on configurable budget and quality tolerances. The detector emits alerts and an evidence bundle used for automated rollbacks.
- Automatic rollback policies: policy DSL to specify when to automatically revert to the last known-good profile. Policies support soft-rollbacks (route 10% of traffic back), canary rollbacks, and immediate full rollback. Rollback actions are idempotent and logged with audit events.
- Zipper quantizer: new quantizer mode that applies quantization in N progressive steps (e.g., 16->8->6->4 bits) and only proceeds to the next step when shadow telemetry stays within bounds for a stabilization window. This reduces large one-shot regressions and makes rollbacks cheap.
- CLI and Console hooks: add tenant-level controls to Redwood Console (read-only telemetry rows during shadowing and a rollback button), and new CLI flags for dry-run and force-apply.
- Telemetry and observability: unit-econ metrics, regression-confidence histograms, and a new prefixed namespace redwood.cost_drift.*. Dashboards and alert rules added under telemetry/playbooks.
- Tests and simulation: includes an offline simulator that replays historical traffic to estimate false-positive risk and a set of unit/integration tests.

Files changed (high level): 
- runtime/drift/investigator.py (core drift detector + policy enforcement)
- runtime/quant/zipper_quant.py (zipper quantizer implementation)
- runtime/shadow/runner.go (lightweight shadow routing and sampling)
- console/src/components/tenantShadow.tsx (Console UI rows and rollback button)
- cli/redwoodctl/cost_drift.go (dry-run/force flags)
- docs/ops/cost-drift.md (operator guide and policy examples)
- telemetry/dashboards/cost-drift-overview.json (dashboard panels)

Migration notes and backwards compatibility: shadowing is opt-in per-tenant by default; existing deployments are unaffected unless operators opt-in. The zipper quantizer is a new mode and does not replace existing quant workflows. Rollbacks are backward-compatible: if rollback engine cannot find prior profile it falls back to strongest safety profile and logs the decision.

Checklist (author): 
- [x] Core detector and policy engine implemented
- [x] Zipper quantizer with step gating
- [x] Console and CLI controls wired
- [x] Telemetry names and dashboards added
- [x] Unit + integration tests
- [x] Offline simulator and sample historical run

Related work and context: Follows on ideas from internal econ-autotune prototypes (ENG-20217) and the tenant warmstart experiments; addresses chronic post-rollout cost spikes seen in Q3 and the incident logged in SUP-4983. This aims to reduce manual rollback toil and decrease mean-time-to-repair for cost regressions.

Risks and mitigations: 
- False-positive rollbacks: mitigated by conservative defaults (soft rollback first + require multiple windows/low p-value) and by the simulator to calibrate thresholds.
- Additional telemetry cost: sampling and lightweight trace encoding keep egress footprint modest; operators can tune sampling rates.

Merge notes: squash-merged to main after approvals. Backported small safety checks to release/2025.11 in follow-up PR.
